summary: Code review PASS. All 5 acceptance criteria met.

_storesDirOverride follows the established test-isolation convention from the TypeScript layer. The JSDoc is clear about its test-only intent. storeInit() correctly threads the override through to saveConfig(), and the third test now directly asserts directory creation.
storeRemove() null-clearing is correctly ordered: empty-stores check (sets null) before same-default check (promotes first remaining). This prevents an array[0] access on an empty array.

One medium-priority design note: leaving { stores: [], default_store: null } triggers a TypeScript schema validation warning on next server load. The server correctly falls to legacy mode, but the warning is noisy. Deleting stores.json when all stores are removed would be a cleaner state transition — out of scope for WP-008.

comments.note: _storesDirOverride follows the established test-isolation convention from the TypeScript layer (configPath override). The JSDoc is clear about its test-only intent. No issues.

When storeRemove() removes the last store and writes { stores: [], default_store: null }, the TypeScript StoresConfigSchema will reject this on next server load (stores must have min(1) and default_store is z.string()). loadStoresConfig() returns null on validation failure (with a stderr warning), so the server falls to legacy single-store mode. This is the intended degraded-state behavior per the WP spec. However, the stderr warning is undesirable and could confuse users. A clean-up option: delete stores.json when stores becomes empty, instead of leaving an invalid file. Medium-priority follow-up.
The storeRemove() null-clearing fix is correctly ordered: empty-stores check (null) before same-default check (first remaining). The else-if ordering prevents a store[0] access on an empty array.
